chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran from Hammad from Hariz from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Zihar (conjugal exile) has two types: one is when he says, 'You are to me like the back of my mother,' and then he remains silent; this is the one that requires expiation before consummation. The other is when he says, 'You are to me like the back of my mother if I do such and such'; if he does it and becomes liable (by fulfilling the condition), then the expiation is upon him at the time he becomes liable.

key_terms.الظِّهَارُ: Zihar, a form of irrevocable separation where the husband compares his wife's back to his mother's back.
key_terms.الْكَفَّارَةُ: Expiation (penance for breaking an oath or specific acts).

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between conditional and unconditional Zihar in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfarayini clarifies the jurisprudential distinction between unconditional and conditional Zihar, emphasizing that the obligation of Kaffarah (expiation) arises at the moment of the 'breaking of the oath' (hanath) rather than merely upon consummation. It highlights the Shia scholarly focus on the precise timing of legal liability in marital separations, linking the concept of Zihar to the broader Islamic legal principle of conditional vows.
